intro: AI engineering, and the place it meets your security work. The crossover is the differentiator: plenty of people build agents and plenty audit contracts, and almost nobody measures an agent doing the auditing.

groups.title: AI engineering
groups.note: Most of these are fellowship labs you are doing anyway. A lab plus a result is an article you already paid for.

items.t: Tool calling breaks on malformed output — what a schema validator actually has to handle
items.d: A two-tool pipeline with strict validation, every malformed response over a hundred runs logged and classified. The taxonomy of failures is the contribution; everyone writes the happy path.

items.t: An MCP server for your own tools, and what exposing them costs you
items.d: Re-expose two tools behind MCP and compare integration effort, latency and failure surface against direct calling. You run MCP in production; the cost side is unwritten.

items.t: The harness is the product: evaluating an agent you built
items.d: Run your auditor against targets you solved by hand and record found, missed and wrongly discarded. That table is the eval harness. Agent demos are everywhere; agent evaluations are not.

items.t: RAG over your own documents, and the retrieval failures nobody screenshots
items.d: Twenty queries it answers wrongly, each classified by cause — chunking, embedding or reranking. The failure gallery is the piece.

items.t: What finetuning actually bought me, measured against a better prompt
items.d: One task, baselined with prompting then finetuned, with cost, latency and quality side by side — including the case where prompting won. The honest negative result is rarer and more linkable.

items.t: Structured outputs: forcing clean JSON out of a model
items.d: Schemas, retries and repair, with the failure rate before and after.

items.t: Context windows, tokens and what you are actually paying for
items.d: Tokenisation made concrete, priced per request, for people who have only seen the marketing number.

items.t: Prompt templates as a library, not as strings in a file
items.d: Versioning, testing and diffing prompts the way you would any other interface.

items.t: Models and hardware: a practical reference
items.d: What runs locally, what needs an API, and the quality cliff between them for your actual workload.

groups.title: AI for security — your differentiator
groups.note: This cluster is the strongest position available to you right now. Nobody credible is publishing honest numbers here.

items.t: I pointed an AI auditor at bugs I had already solved by hand. Here is what it missed.
items.d: Five hand-solved targets, with found, missed and wrongly discarded published, plus the PoC prompt that failed in each case. Every AI audit tool publishes what it found; none publish what they missed.

items.t: The discard pile is the product: tuning an AI auditor's false-positive gate
items.d: Open a run's discards, decide for each whether the gate was right or the prompt failed, and make one tuning change justified by a specific discard. The commit is the artifact.

items.t: Turning a Solodit finding into an executable invariant
items.d: Ten findings restated as assertions a fuzzer can break. 'Accounting should be correct' is not an invariant; 'totalBorrows + cash == totalSupplied - reserves' is.

items.t: Browsing for bugs: what the Zellic Premia find teaches about agent-assisted auditing
items.d: Read their $3M write-up as a method, then try the method on a live scope and report whether it transfers.

items.t: Writing a detector: Cyfrin's detector API in practice
items.d: Build one real detector for a bug class you have seen twice, and measure its false-positive rate on real code.

items.t: AI-assisted CTF solving: where it helps and where it hallucinates
items.d: Run an agent at CTF levels you have already solved, and classify its reasoning failures.

groups.title: Twelve-week AI roadmap
groups.note: Preserved from the previous version of this tab. Each week: study, a small build, an article and a video, producing one public deliverable.

items.t: Week 1 — Foundations: LLM basics and prompt engineering
items.d: Study tokens, context windows and sampling. Build a tiny CLI that calls an LLM API. Deliverable: prompt-cli repo, blog post, 5-minute video.

items.t: Week 2 — APIs and structured outputs
items.d: Study JSON mode, temperature and retries. Build an API wrapper that always returns valid JSON. Deliverable: public wrapper repo plus an 8-minute video.

items.t: Week 3 — Prompt templates for real primitives
items.d: Templates for email, hero copy and summaries. Build a prompt library with a small web UI. Deliverable: a deployed site plus blog post.

items.t: Week 4 — Retrieval basics
items.d: Embeddings, chunking and vector stores. Build search over your own notes. Deliverable: repo plus a write-up of what retrieval got wrong.

items.t: Week 5 — RAG end to end
items.d: Reranking and citation. Build RAG that cites its sources. Deliverable: a demo plus the failure gallery.

items.t: Week 6 — Tool calling and MCP
items.d: Function schemas, validation and error handling. Build a two-tool pipeline, then expose it behind MCP. Deliverable: repo plus the integration comparison.

items.t: Week 7 — Agents and loops
items.d: Planning, memory and termination. Build an agent that completes a multi-step task. Deliverable: repo plus a post on where the loop fails.

items.t: Week 8 — Evaluation
items.d: Building a harness, scoring, and regression tests for prompts. Deliverable: the eval harness as a repo — this is the week that matters most.

items.t: Week 9 — Finetuning
items.d: When it beats prompting, and the dataset work it actually requires. Deliverable: a measured comparison.

items.t: Week 10 — Dataset engineering
items.d: Collection, cleaning and labelling, with the cost per example written down. Deliverable: a documented dataset.

items.t: Week 11 — Deployment and cost
items.d: Latency, caching, batching and spend per request. Deliverable: a deployed service with a cost model.

items.t: Week 12 — Applying it to security
items.d: Point everything built so far at the auditor. Deliverable: the agent evaluation that anchors the whole series.
